sections.html:
Merrillville is a town in Ross Township, Lake County, part of the Chicago metro area in Northwest Indiana. It grew up at the crossing of Interstate 65 and U.S. Route 30, spreads over about 33.3 square miles and touches Gary, Hobart, Winfield, Crown Point, Schererville and Griffith.

The 2020 census counted 36,444 residents, up from 35,246 in 2010 and 30,560 in 2000, and the 2025 estimate is 37,407. Since January 2015 Merrillville has been the most populous town in Indiana. It is run by a town manager rather than a mayor. Median household income is $62,221 and median age is 40.0.

sections.h2: What shapes demand for Merrillville houses
sections.html:
Merrillville is a retail hub for the region. Big-box stores, hotels, restaurants and car dealers line the U.S. 30 corridor between Taft Street and Colorado Street. NiSource, White Lodging and Centier Bank all have their headquarters in town, and Ameriplex at the Crossroads, an industrial and technology park, sits on Broadway.

Steel and refining belong to other parts of Lake County, not to Merrillville itself. Lake effect snow, cold winters and warm summers are hard on roofs, gutters, sump pumps and furnaces, and a house with deferred maintenance shows it quickly. Buyers who finance with a mortgage tend to ask for those items to be fixed, which is one reason sellers consider a direct purchase.

Your tax bill and your deed go through Lake County, not the town. The county seat is Crown Point. That is where the Treasurer is located, and the Auditor's tax sales office is at 2293 North Main Street, Building A, 2nd Floor, phone 219-755-3155, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The town handles building and zoning. Call the county for taxes and recording, and the town for permits and rental questions.

The Planning and Building Department enforces Merrillville's building codes and zoning ordinances. It is at 7820 Broadway, Merrillville, IN 46410. The department phone is 219-769-3631 and the town main line is 219-769-5711.

The department's documents page offers a rental registration application, along with contractor, variance and subdivision forms. If you rent out the house you plan to sell, ask the department whether your registration is current before closing. Call as well about permits, fees and any certificate of occupancy rule that applies to your address, since the steps depend on the property.

Open permits and unfinished work are worth checking even on an owner-occupied house. A buyer's title company or inspector may ask about them, and sorting them out early prevents a delay on closing day.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and tax sales
sections.html:
Indiana Code 6-1.1-22-9 sets two installments, on May 10 and November 10. The Lake County Treasurer posts the exact schedule and payment options each year.

Lake County sells tax-delinquent parcels at an online auction run through zeusauction.com. The 2026 sale ran from Friday, September 4 through Tuesday, September 8, with registration set at $100. If taxes on your house have fallen behind, check the sale calendar before you pick a closing date, because a sale that settles the balance in time keeps the parcel off the auction block.

Ask the Auditor's tax sales office at 219-755-3155 what is owed and whether your parcel is on a list.

sections.h2: How deeds are handled in Lake County
sections.html:
Before the deed goes to the auditor, the seller and buyer complete a sales disclosure form under Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5-3, and the county assessor has to approve the form first. One form covers contiguous parcels in the same taxing district when they transfer on a single deed.

A title company usually handles the filing, so you mostly sign and confirm who is on the deed.

Owners sell for many reasons: a move, an inheritance, trouble with a rental or the cost of repairs. In each case the choice is between listing and a direct sale.

  • Listing means preparing the house, scheduling showings and waiting on a buyer's financing and inspection.
  • A cash purchase takes the house as it stands, and you set the closing date.

Compare net proceeds, timing and effort across the options before you decide.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale close in Merrillville?
sections.html:
1. Tell us the address, who is on the deed and the condition of the house, including tenants and any open town notices.
  2. Receive a written offer and take whatever time you need to compare it with listing.
  3. If you accept, a title company opens the file, searches the title and confirms what is owed on taxes and any mortgage.
  4. You and the buyer sign the sales disclosure form and the deed, and the title company records the transfer with Lake County.
  5. Back taxes, liens and a mortgage payoff are paid from the proceeds, and the balance goes to you.

Useful papers to have ready include the deed, a recent tax bill, the lease if the house is rented and any letter from the Planning and Building Department. Because there is no lender, the closing date depends on the title work and on your own schedule.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or a house with repair needs
sections.html: A cash buyer can purchase a house without repairs, and you choose the closing date. If tenants live there, bring the lease and tell the buyer what the lease says about the end date. Confirm your rental registration with the Planning and Building Department at 219-769-3631 so the file is clean when the title company reviews it.

faqs.q: Is Merrillville a city or a town?
faqs.a: Merrillville is a town in Lake County, governed under Indiana law with a town manager. It was incorporated in 1971 and is the most populous town in Indiana.

faqs.q: Do Merrillville landlords have to register rentals?
faqs.a: The town's planning and building documents page offers a rental registration application. Call the department at 219-769-3631 to confirm the current requirements for your house.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lake County?
faqs.a: State law sets May 10 and November 10. The county treasurer posts the exact schedule and payment options.

faqs.q: Which county office do I call about my deed?
faqs.a: Lake County handles recording and the sales disclosure form, with Crown Point as the county seat. A title company normally does the filing for you.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Merrillville house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it without repairs, and you choose the closing date.
